title: SecOps-NG Crypto Attestation Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the crypto-attestation evidence stream (F-CP-05). One artifact is produced per workflow execution and attests, mechanically, that (a) no secret material was baked into the workflow's compiled code, (b) every secret the workflow consumes is injected via the runtime environment at boot, and (c) the named environment variables the workflow references are captured by name only — never by value. The artifact pins those assertions against the workflow's run identifier, the compile target that produced the running form, and the capture timestamp, so a reviewer can correlate the assertion back to a specific execution and a specific compiled artifact. Downstream consumers are the NIS2 Article 21(2)(h) cryptography-and-encryption mapping and Core Directive #6 (secret management). Public-bar artifact: env-var references MUST stay SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE names only — env-var values, key material, and credential-shaped strings are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<compile_target>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Deterministic on those three inputs so a replay of the same execution re-derives the same id and dedup is trivial.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable identifier of the workflow whose execution this attestation covers. Convention: lower-snake-case workflow stable-id from `content/playbooks/<workflow>/` (e.g. `incident_management`, `vulnerability_triage`). Joins back into the workflow content layer so a reviewer can re-derive which playbook was compiled into the running form.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Each execution emits its own attestation — re-runs of the same workflow produce distinct execution_ids and distinct artifact_ids.

compile_target.description: Which of the three reference compile targets produced the running form of the workflow. The attestation is target-specific because the compiled artifact differs per target (n8n JSON, Temporal Python class, LangGraph state graph) and the env-only injection path is verified per target. Constrained to the three reference targets the project ships compilers for; community-contributed targets are out of scope for this enum.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (typically `nis2:art-21-2-h`). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP-05 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses. At least one — typically `control.crypto_policy_inventory@v1` and/or a future `control.secret_handling@v1` once the F-PT-01 platform card lands it.

secret_handling.description: The three mechanical assertions that make this a crypto-attestation: (a) no secret material was baked into the compiled workflow, (b) all secrets the workflow consumes are injected via the runtime environment, (c) the env-vars the workflow references are captured by name only. The booleans are typed-`const` on the affirmative value so a careless emitter writing `false` (i.e. asserting that a secret WAS baked in, or that injection went through some non-env path) fails schema validation at the emitter boundary. The F-PT-01 refuse-at-boot enforcement is downstream of this assertion — the schema captures the assertion shape, the platform guarantees it.

secrets_baked_in.description: Affirmative assertion that no secret material is baked into the workflow's compiled code. The schema pins this to `false` — any artifact claiming otherwise is rejected at the schema boundary, on the grounds that an attestation asserting a baked-in secret is not the artifact F-CP-05 ships, it is a vulnerability disclosure for F-CP-04.

injection_mode.description: How secrets reach the workflow at runtime. Constant on `env` — the F-CP-05 stream attests environment-variable injection at boot, no other injection path. A future schema revision may broaden the vocabulary if the platform supports additional sovereign paths (e.g. mounted secrets file with the same refuse-at-boot guarantee); until then this is a single-value enum on purpose.

env_var_refs.description: The named environment variables the workflow references for secret material. Names only — values, fragments of values, or any credential-shaped strings are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and Core Directive #6, and the regex below rejects anything that is not an UPPER_SNAKE_CASE identifier. Empty list is valid (a workflow that consumes no secrets still emits an attestation to that effect).

secret_count.description: Optional pre-computed count of distinct env-var references the workflow consumes (== `len(env_var_refs)`). Carried so downstream rollups skip re-derivation. Reviewer-side correctness check, not schema-enforced.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this attestation was captured. Carried into `artifact_id`-adjacent dedup decisions by the emitter; not part of artifact_id itself (which is derived from workflow_id + execution_id + compile_target so re-emissions in the same execution stay byte-identical).

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

owner.description: Optional dated ownership pointer for the secret-handling posture this attestation covers. Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline. Optional at this layer because the F-CP-05 attestation is a per-execution mechanical assertion; the owning role typically lives on the upstream `control.crypto_policy_inventory@v1` entry.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'platform-security-wg', 'secrets-custodian@example.org'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of the secret-handling posture.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration, defaulted by the operator's configuration.
